newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Ferrum wants to rise '97 exports to 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish Ferrum wants to rise '97 exports to 8.5 pct.

text.p: Polish pipe maker Huta Ferrum SA, which starts its initial public offering on Tuesday, expects to increase its exports to 8.5 percent of sales in 1997 from six percent in 1996, the firm's president said on Monday.
"In 1997 we plan exports growth to 8.5 percent...we want our products to be present on many foreign markets," Jan Korzeniec told a news conference.

The company, which has 28 percent of the domestic pipe market expected its net profit to rise to 4.8 million zlotys this year on 165-million-zloty sales, up from last year's 2.9-million-zloty net on 148-million-zloty sales.
Korzeniec said thanks to planned investments and introducing new products the company should be able to increase its exports to central European countries and the Far East.
Currently the firm, which is seeking a main market listing, exports its products mainly to Denmark, Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia and Austria, he said.
Hubert Janiszewski, head of financial adviser HSBC Investment Services, also present, said his firm had underwritten two million shares of Ferrum's three-million-share offering.
He said Polish Development Bank PBR underwrote one million shares and the stand-by fee was three percent.
Janiszewski also said the Polish National Investment Fund No 1 (NFI 1), which currently holds a 33-percent stake in Ferrum, was likely to buy shares of the new issue, but he did not know how many.
Ferrum's other shareholders are 14 National Investment Funds holding 27 percent of shares, the state treasury with 25 percent and the firm's employees with 15 percent.
